samples.marker: LockBit 3 Black: add aPLib decompressor coverage
evidence: PE32 LockBit Black ransomware, rather than a miner inferred from the collection filename.
ROR13 hashes seeded by lowercased module-name hashes and XOR-hidden API tables resolve CreateFileW, ReadFile, WriteFile, MoveFileExW, and I/O completion APIs.

Worker at VA 0x46ddd4 dequeues completion packets, reads the file at 0x46de77, transforms its buffer through 0x4620bc at 0x46df2a, and rewrites it through WriteFile at 0x46dfa1. File preparation at 0x46eec8 renames, opens, and queues files.

Emulated only pure arithmetic/decompression helpers: XOR 0x30 reveals compressed helper code, aPLib decompression recovers the 64-bit LCG helper, and the state-dependent XOR routine at 0x461730 recovers encrypted strings and configuration. The configuration is additionally aPLib-compressed and contains Base64 fields.
Decoded UTF-16 extortion text at VA 0x47b004 identifies LockBit Black and states that important files are encrypted. Its assertion that files were stolen is not treated as proof of exfiltration.
Added neutral x86 aPLib decompressor coverage; existing ransomware identity and hidden API-trampoline traits are supported.

samples.marker: ARM IRC flood bot: detect encrypted C2; fix mode-name FPs
evidence: Static ARM/uClibc IRC-controlled multi-vector DDoS bot; no narrower named malware family established.

IRC receive/negotiation path at 0x0000faa8 processes PING and CRYPT frames. CRYPT handling at 0x0000fcfc parses 24 bytes of hexadecimal negotiation material, derives separate ircd-tx and ircd-rx keys, and initializes directional cipher state at 0x0000fe58 and 0x0000fe68.

Remote command dispatcher 0x00010320 reaches flood dispatcher 0x000085a0. It parses mode, target, port and optional arguments, selects TCP/UDP/GRE and bypass attack handlers, and schedules flood workers. Raw socket creation and ARM networking syscall wrappers corroborate packet generation.

Process name is set to [kworker/0:1]; hidden helper paths and shell command templates provide concealment and remote administration context. The lab-test-bot registration label does not override these execution paths.

The bare killall and discord strings at VA 0x2b56c and 0x2b600 are compared as attack selectors, not executed as killall or used as a Discord application path. Removed these false interpretations by tightening capability matchers.

Added encrypted IRC negotiation coverage, moved the generic ARM kill syscall to process signal control, and removed an alias that incorrectly filed ordinary PATH assignment under privilege escalation.

samples.marker: SNOWLIGHT ARM loader: remove unsupported VShell attribution
evidence: Dynamically linked ARM Thumb ELF SNOWLIGHT-style anonymous-stage loader; the supplied Mirai tag is not supported by this executable.
Main at 0x000106a8 exits if /tmp/log_de.log exists, resolves a configured host and connects a TCP socket. The request is formatted at 0x00010750 and sent at 0x0001075e.
At 0x0001076e it consumes HTTP headers through the CRLF-CRLF delimiter. At 0x000107a4 it invokes ARM syscall 385 (memfd_create) with flag 1.
At 0x000107b8 it receives chunks; 0x000107cc XORs every byte with 0x99; 0x000107e0 writes the decoded buffer to the anonymous fd held in r7.
At 0x000107f8 it obtains its own canonical path and exports it through setenv. At 0x0001080e it constructs argv with [kworker/0:2] and at 0x0001081e passes the same anonymous fd to fexecve.

This establishes covert acquired-code execution and kernel-worker masquerade. No fetched payload was available; VShell behavior or identity is not inferred from the spoofed process name. Removed the redundant VShell family atom and reused the neutral process-name observation in its existing composite.
Moved the symmetric Thumb XOR loop into direction-neutral data encoding; the consuming loader retains its independently established reconstruction context.
